name: Spider Woman (Naʼashjéʼii Asdzą́ą́)

domain_history.domain: advisor/teacher figure to the Hero Twins and to the people generally; credited with teaching weaving and agricultural arts — explicitly NOT the creator of humans in Diné tradition (unlike the Hopi Spider Grandmother/Kokyangwuti, a creator figure in that separate tradition)

notes: In some recorded Navajo tellings, Spider Woman is herself described as a Kisani (Pueblo) woman who was taught weaving by a spider — the tradition's own internal narrative gestures at a Puebloan point of origin for the weaving-teaching motif, consistent with the broader documented pattern of post-1680 Puebloan-Navajo religious exchange (see cul_dine notes). The parallel to Hopi/Keresan Spider Grandmother figures is a real, documented shared-figure pattern with a real, documented functional difference (creator in Hopi tradition vs. helper/teacher in Diné tradition) — the causal "borrowed from Pueblo religion" framing is this project's own inference from two independently documented adjacent facts, not a scholar's stated direct claim, and is flagged as such.
